To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

tRNA and ribosome translocation is accompanied by cyclic rotations of the large and small subunits of the ribosome around the axis of intersublunit interface and that the translocation process requires the presence of the GTPase EF‐G in the A site of small subunit.

tRNA and messenger RNA (mRNA) translocation within the bacterial ribosome is accompanied cyclic forward and reverse intersubunit rotations and forward‐ and backswiveling motions of the head domain of the small ribosome subunit.

ribosome translocation involves cyclic forward and reverse intersubunit rotations and forward–back swivels of the head of the small subunit, which are driven by the binding of domain IV of the GTPase EF‐G to the ribosome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of ribosome trans‐ and dissociation, the role of the ribosome in protein synthesis, and the role of the tRNA and mRNA in ribosome translocation.
the structural and functional characterization of the bacterial ribosome and the ribosome‐associated protein factors, which play key roles in translation
understanding the structural basis of protein synthesis in ribosomes, which is a fundamental process in all living cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mechanism of tRNA/mRNAS translocation within the bacterial ribosome is a complex and highly coordinated process involving multiple structural changes of the ribosome itself as well as of its translocase, elongation factors G and G′, and is not fully understood.
EF‐G induces tRNA translocation by the cyclic forward‐ and back rotations of the large and small subunit around the intersubunit axis.

ribosome translocation is a highly dynamic process that is coupled to a number of conformational changes of the ribosome itself, tRNAs, mRNA and EF‐G.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we know the mechanism of ribosome translation, but not the mechanism of ribosomal translation.
the ribosome is a highly dynamic machine that is capable of performing a number of conformational changes during the elongation phase of protein synthesis.
ribosome translocation is a complex molecular process, which involves the coordinated motion of the ribosome subunits and the ribosome‐associated factors, such as elongation factors and tRNAs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the translocation mechanism of the ribosome is more complex than it appears to be.

the ribosome and its translocase EF‐G undergo a complex series of structural rearrangments during ribosome translocaiton, which are coupled to the forward translocation motion of tRNA and mRNA inside the ribosome.
the ribosome is a highly dynamic molecular machine that undergoes cyclic rotations and swivels during the process of translocation.
